trickyParts: The plan's own TestAnApprovalEndsTheRoundWhateverCISays rows are unreachable under the plan's reviewRound ordering (roundApproved then roundSentBack): with a red standing, whichever half arrives first finds the round incomplete, falls through to RedSendsBack and sends the work back, and the second half is refused HANDOFF_NOT_CURRENT_PHASE (that is exactly the row's failure on main). So the round reads no CI at all; standingRed holds the CI rule and the push handler and the hold retry apply it before asking the round.

Deleting decideChecks' reviewing branch removed the only path that re-evaluated a round left open by CodeOnItsWay once the push's new head arrived (the new head's settlement used to). pullRequestSynchronized now re-asks the round in reviewing, guarded on HeadPushKnown: GitHub delivers push and synchronize in either order, and asking before the push is classified would re-tell a stuck round at the new head for a handoff push that then ends it approved (TestAHeadArrivingBeforeItsPushTellsNothingOfAStuckRound).

retro → implementing is a same-role move: record.SuperviseRequest validation refuses a start whose Quiesce is its own role, so takenOver returns no quiesce when the leaving role is the starting one; the implementer keeps its turn and is handed the implementing task once it ends.

The daemon's tests need Postgres: an embedded Postgres 16.4 from the zonky jar (docs/solutions/testing/…LEGION-668.md) at 127.0.0.1:54331; the NATS-backed tests are skipped by name (-skip 'Consume|Captured|RateLimited|BackwardMoveNoRow|LateEventOfAnEarlier|ScratchDispatch'), and ./internal/daemon runs by -run selection. CI's Tests run 38521728279 ran them all green.

Round 2: the push handler's one guard served two rules - the CI rule and the round's re-ask - so a late push that completed a red's carry acted only in reviewing. standingRed now excludes awaiting_merge itself (a carried red must not withdraw a READY GitHub judged on the head's own CI; sendBack would otherwise find the awaiting_merge checks_red row), so every caller gets the one rule, and the re-ask alone stays reviewing's.

Round 3: the reviewer's two Important findings were the remaining facts that can make a red stand without applying the rule - the synchronize completing a carry (the push's mirror image) and a hold retried from a phase other than reviewing. Both now call standingRed first; the rule's doc states the invariant (whichever fact makes a red stand applies it, never a review or a completion) instead of listing facts, so the next such fact has a sentence to be measured against.
deviations: Plan §1/D1 kept a roundSentBack case inside reviewRound after roundApproved. The implementation takes the CI read out of reviewRound entirely (standingRed, applied by decideChecks, the push classification handler and the hold retry before the round is asked). On the review and completion facts D1 holds literally: a red already standing when the approval lands is unsent and the issue goes to retro (R1's window). The asymmetry, chosen with the architect (2026-10-14): a hold retry or a push classification that finds BOTH an approval and a standing red sends the work to implementing, where plan D1 said retro — Sami's two rules are independent and name no order, a red head would reach READY only to be refused, so implementing is the cheaper outcome. An oracle pass found no fact outside those four that can newly make a red sendable, so nothing the plan's roundSentBack caught is lost.

pullRequestSynchronized re-asks the review round in reviewing on a head's arrival once its push is known (not in the plan): the replacement for decideChecks' deleted reviewing branch, which re-evaluated a round left open by CodeOnItsWay at the new head's settlement.
handoff_test.go's TestApprovalBeforeGreenChecksAdvancesWhenTheChecksSettle (not on the plan's list) asserted 'reviewing until green' and is now TestAnApprovalBeforeTheChecksSettleAdvancesWithoutThem.

The 'in merging' checks-red rows seed status 'retro' (merging sets no Dispatch status of its own); the completion-then-approval rows of TestAnApprovalEndsTheRoundWhateverCISays assert exactly one review-stuck notice (a completion before its decision has always told once), where the plan said none; the approval-first rows assert zero.
The daemon's TestAFailedRequiredWorkflowSendsTheWorkBack is kept, reduced (no declared column, plus a 'failed, in retro' row) rather than deleted.

Acceptance 6's grep is not literally empty: its only allowed hits are the refusal's own text — config_test.go's two refusal rows and running-legion.md's Upgrade note (plan T7). Any other hit fails it. Agreed with the architect.

The planner's committed .legion/LEGION-698/plan.json:38 named the other deployment's project name, which .github/scripts/check-private-names.sh (the required lint job) refuses; one word is redacted in a commit of mine, the planner's commit untouched.

The deploy ordering (plan §6): the other deployment's legion.yaml sets review_workflows and the new daemon refuses to boot on it; the architect settled on the plan thread that the legion-deploy holder drops the key in the same pull request as the pin after the release.
